records.context: The warm-up polishes before it shows. Qt posts every new widget a ``PolishRequest``, and a dialog built ahead in an idle slice (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) answers it in the next pass of the event loop, long before :meth:`setVisible`. The window sheet and the glass then walked all ~967 widgets of every tab in that one event: 425-484 ms offscreen, 0.36 s on the lesson capture host. The pages leave here as they would at the show, and the polish styles the open tab only.
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences._preferences_window_class._PreferencesWindow.event#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: THE WARM-UP POLISHES BEFORE IT SHOWS. Qt posts every new widget a ``PolishRequest``, and a dialog built ahead in an idle slice (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) answers it in the next pass of the event loop, long before :meth:`setVisible`. The window sheet and the glass then walked all ~967 widgets of every tab in that one event: 425-484 ms offscreen, 0.36 s on the lesson capture host. The pages leave here as they would at the show, and the polish styles the open tab only.
records.translation: warm-up दिखाने से पहले polish करता है। Qt हर नए विजेट को एक ``PolishRequest`` भेजता है, और idle समय में पहले से बनाया गया डायलॉग (:func:`_warm_the_preferences`) event loop के अगले pass में, :meth:`setVisible` से बहुत पहले, उसका उत्तर देता है। window sheet और glass तब उसी एक event में हर टैब के लगभग ~967 विजेट पर चलते थे: offscreen 425-484 ms, lesson capture host पर 0.36 s। पेज यहाँ से वैसे ही जाते हैं जैसे दिखाते समय जाते, और polish केवल खुले टैब को शैली देता है।

records.context: Only for a dialog the warm-up built, which says so through ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish``. Anything else that builds the dialog and lets the event loop run before walking a page -- the help search index reads every tab's form rows that way -- still finds every page where the builder put it until the show.
records.label: spacr.qt.preferences._preferences_window_class._PreferencesWindow.event#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ONLY FOR A DIALOG THE WARM-UP BUILT, which says so through ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish``. Anything else that builds the dialog and lets the event loop run before walking a page -- the help search index reads every tab's form rows that way -- still finds every page where the builder put it until the show.
records.translation: केवल उस डायलॉग के लिए जिसे warm-up ने बनाया, जो ``_pages_leave_at_the_polish`` से यह बताता है। डायलॉग बनाने वाली और किसी पेज पर चलने से पहले event loop चलने देने वाली कोई भी अन्य चीज़ -- help search index हर टैब की फ़ॉर्म पंक्तियाँ इसी तरह पढ़ता है -- दिखाए जाने तक हर पेज को वहीं पाती है जहाँ builder ने उसे रखा।

records.context: Read by :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png`, which is the single consumer. ``pdf`` makes it write a vector page beside the display raster; the work list then rasterises that page for a crisper view and the user has a file that opens as editable art. records.context: What this reaches and what it does not. It is the colour of the figure's CHROME: the axis spines and the tick marks. It is deliberately not pushed over the data's own lines on every render, because a preference that repainted every series in one ink would flatten every multi-series figure in the package the first time a theme was read. The control that DOES reach the data's lines is the per-figure one (:func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_settings.apply_line_colour`), which is a user asking for it about one figure -- the same division as the pyqtgraph side, where the theme sets `_foreground` and `set_line_colour` is a menu entry.

records.source: WHAT THIS REACHES AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It is the colour of the figure's CHROME: the axis spines and the tick marks. records.context: Two consumers, and they treat it differently on purpose. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` clamps it for the on-application view raster — a 16x12" figure at 300 DPI is a 4800 px PNG that costs more to decode than any application view can show — so a large figure is displayed at a lower DPI than the one chosen here. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` uses the value unclamped, because the PDF is a file rather than a screenful and its embedded rasters really do need the resolution the user asked for.

records.source: Two consumers, and they treat it differently on purpose. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` clamps it for the on-screen raster — a 16x12" figure at 300 DPI is a 4800 px PNG that costs more to decode than any screen can show — so a large figure is displayed at a lower DPI than the one chosen here. :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` uses the value unclamped, because the PDF is a file rather than a screenful and its embedded rasters really do need the resolution the user asked for.
records.translation: दो उपभोक्ता, और वे इसे जानबूझकर अलग तरह से लेते हैं। :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue.render_figure_to_png` on-screen raster के लिए इसे सीमित करता है — 300 DPI पर 16x12" figure एक 4800 px PNG है जिसे डिकोड करने में किसी भी स्क्रीन के दिखा सकने से अधिक लागत आती है — इसलिए बड़ा figure यहाँ चुने गए DPI से कम पर दिखाया जाता है। :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.figure_queue._export_vector_pdf` मान को बिना सीमित किए उपयोग करता है, क्योंकि PDF एक फ़ाइल है, स्क्रीन भर का दृश्य नहीं, और उसके embedded rasters को वास्तव में वही resolution चाहिए जो उपयोगकर्ता ने माँगा।

records.context: A suggestion is judged, not relabelled. An extracted image region Suggest proposed a class for wears an amber ``?`` badge beside its dashed ring. A click or ``Y`` confirms it (it becomes an ordinary label and wears a green tick); a right-click or ``N`` rejects it (it goes back to unanswered and wears a red cross); ``U`` undoes either. The bar above the structured-data name legend says so, and counts what the page and the column hold. Each judgement is written to the ``<column>_verdict`` column as ``+c`` or ``-c``, so it survives a restart, and the next Suggest round is handed the rejections to train on. See :meth:`AnnotateScreen._judge` and :func:`spacr.suggest.verdict_column`.

records.context: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary structured-data name. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite stores ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column without error; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#14

records.source: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. records.translation: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` चालू होना चाहिए — यह डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से बंद है और Preferences में है, यहाँ इस browser में नहीं। 2. डेटाबेस इस सत्र में स्पष्ट रूप से चुना गया होना चाहिए (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``)। 3. उपयोगकर्ता को "Edit mode" पर tick करना *और* पुष्टि करनी होगी; केवल tick करने से कुछ नहीं होता। 4. पंक्ति ``rowid`` या primary key से पहचानी जा सकने वाली होनी चाहिए। उसके बिना संपादन अस्वीकार किया जाता है — कॉलम मानों पर मेल करने वाला UPDATE कई पंक्तियों पर लग सकता है, जो माप तालिका पर मौन सामूहिक दूषण है। लेखन पहले पंक्ति पते के लिए ``COUNT(*)`` भी जाँचता है और ``rowcount == 1`` न होने पर rollback करता है। 5. टाइप किया गया टेक्स्ट कॉलम के घोषित प्रकार में बदला जा सकने वाला होना चाहिए। SQLite INTEGER कॉलम में ``'abc'`` बिना त्रुटि के संग्रहीत करता है; :func:`coerce_for_column` इसके बजाय अस्वीकार करता है।

records.context: Design notes that matter for real spaCR databases:
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Design notes that matter for real spaCR databases:
records.translation: वास्तविक spaCR डेटाबेस के लिए महत्वपूर्ण डिज़ाइन टिप्पणियाँ:

records.context: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. Only tables with no usable structured-data name (views, composite-primary-structured-data name ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1. Only tables with no usable key (views, composite-primary-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.translation: **Keyset paging, OFFSET नहीं।** हर chunk ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` और ``ORDER BY rowid`` माँगता है। ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` SQLite से हर छोड़ी गई पंक्ति पर चलवाता (और उसे फेंकवाता) है, इसलिए 400 k-row तालिका का chunk 500, chunk 1 से 500× महँगा होता। केवल बिना उपयोग योग्य कुंजी वाली तालिकाएँ (views, composite-primary-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` तालिकाएँ) ``OFFSET`` पर लौटती हैं, और वे स्वभाव से छोटी होती हैं।

records.context: **The count never blocks the first paint.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` is a full scan. The first chunk is painted against ``max(rowid)``, which is O(1), and that number is *always* rendered as "≈… (estimate)". The exact ``COUNT(*)`` follows on its own job and replaces it.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The count never blocks the first paint.** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` is a full scan. The first chunk is painted against ``max(rowid)``, which is O(1), and that number is *always* rendered as "≈… (estimate)". The exact ``COUNT(*)`` follows on its own job and replaces it.
records.translation: **गिनती कभी पहले paint को नहीं रोकती।** ``SELECT COUNT(*)`` एक पूरा scan है। पहला chunk ``max(rowid)`` के सापेक्ष पेंट किया जाता है, जो O(1) है, और वह संख्या *हमेशा* "≈… (estimate)" के रूप में दिखाई जाती है। सटीक ``COUNT(*)`` अपने अलग job पर आता है और उसका स्थान लेता है।

records.context: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. Results tagged with a stale token are dropped, so an in-flight load can never paint the previous table's rows into the new view, and a job that has not started yet is dropped without spending an independent execution path. Nothing is ever killed mid-flight.
records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Cancellable.** Switching table or database bumps a load token. Results tagged with a stale token are dropped, so an in-flight load can never paint the previous table's rows into the new view, and a job that has not started yet is dropped without spending a thread. Nothing is ever killed mid-flight.
records.translation: **रद्द करने योग्य।** तालिका या डेटाबेस बदलने से load token बढ़ता है। पुराने token वाले परिणाम हटा दिए जाते हैं, इसलिए चल रहा load कभी पिछली तालिका की पंक्तियाँ नए view में पेंट नहीं कर सकता, और जो job अभी शुरू नहीं हुआ वह थ्रेड खर्च किए बिना हटा दिया जाता है। बीच में कुछ भी कभी kill नहीं किया जाता।

records.context: **Brush** and **Erase** paint and unpaint the active label a pixel at a time. **Erase object** removes a whole label in one click. **Wand** grows a region from the pixel clicked and adds it to the mask by default. Hold Ctrl while clicking to remove that region; the tolerance is relative to the image's intensity range by default, see :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`. **Draw** traces a free-form outline that closes and fills as ONE object -- the tool a brush is not, because a brush stamps disks along the path, so tracing a rim with it labels the rim and leaves the middle background. **Divide / Merge** uses a left-button drag to divide and a right-button drag to merge crossed objects under the first touched identifier without changing their pixels. The merged identity is retained when saving and reopening. Dividing drags a line across a merged object and makes it two, keeping the original identifier on the larger component and giving the smaller a new one, with every other object untouched; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` is the cut width. **Zoom** rectangle-drags the view and changes no labels at all.

records.translation: **Brush** और **Erase** सक्रिय लेबल को एक-एक पिक्सेल करके पेंट करते और मिटाते हैं। **Erase object** एक क्लिक में पूरा लेबल हटाता है। **Wand** क्लिक किए गए पिक्सेल से एक क्षेत्र बढ़ाता है और डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से उसे मास्क में जोड़ता है। उस क्षेत्र को हटाने के लिए क्लिक करते समय Ctrl दबाए रखें; tolerance डिफ़ॉल्ट रूप से इमेज की तीव्रता रेंज के सापेक्ष है, देखें :func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.relative_tolerance`। **Draw** एक मुक्त-रूप रूपरेखा बनाता है जो बंद होकर एक ही ऑब्जेक्ट के रूप में भर जाती है -- यह वह टूल है जो brush नहीं है, क्योंकि brush पथ के साथ डिस्क छापता है, इसलिए उससे किनारा बनाने पर किनारा लेबल होता है और बीच का भाग बैकग्राउंड रहता है। **Divide / Merge** विभाजन के लिए बाएँ बटन से drag और पार किए गए ऑब्जेक्टों को पहले छुए गए पहचानकर्ता के अंतर्गत, उनके पिक्सेल बदले बिना, merge करने के लिए दाएँ बटन से drag का उपयोग करता है। merge की गई पहचान सहेजने और फिर से खोलने पर बनी रहती है। विभाजन में merge किए गए ऑब्जेक्ट के आर-पार एक रेखा खींची जाती है और वह दो बन जाता है, बड़े घटक पर मूल पहचानकर्ता रहता है और छोटे को नया मिलता है, बाकी हर ऑब्जेक्ट अछूता रहता है; :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.DIVIDE_CUT_WIDTH` कट की चौड़ाई है। **Zoom** आयत खींचकर view बदलता है और कोई लेबल नहीं बदलता।

records.context: **Recrop** is the ninth and is the only one that changes WHICH field is on application view rather than what is painted on it. A staged extracted image region holding several cells is not one training example, and curating it as one teaches a network that two objects are one picture -- so a box round an object writes that region of both the image and the mask as a field of its own (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.write_recrop`), queued straight after the current field, and the multi-object original is retired into ``recropped_originals/`` rather than curated (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.retire_recropped_original`). A box shorter than :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MIN_SIDE` on a side, or repeating a cut already made past :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MAX_OVERLAP`, is refused; objects the box cuts through are dropped, because an object whose boundary is where the mouse was released is not that object; and the labels that survive are renumbered from one.

records.source: **Recrop** is the ninth and is the only one that changes WHICH field is on screen rather than what is painted on it. A staged crop holding several cells is not one training example, and curating it as one teaches a network that two objects are one picture -- so a box round an object writes that region of both the image and the mask as a field of its own (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.write_recrop`), queued straight after the current field, and the multi-object original is retired into ``recropped_originals/`` rather than curated (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.retire_recropped_original`). A box shorter than :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MIN_SIDE` on a side, or repeating a cut already made past :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MAX_OVERLAP`, is refused; objects the box cuts through are dropped, because an object whose boundary is where the mouse was released is not that object; and the labels that survive are renumbered from one.
records.translation: **Recrop** नौवाँ टूल है और एकमात्र ऐसा है जो यह बदलता है कि स्क्रीन पर कौन-सा फ़ील्ड है, न कि उस पर क्या पेंट है। कई कोशिकाओं वाला staged क्रॉप एक प्रशिक्षण उदाहरण नहीं है, और उसे एक के रूप में curate करने से network सीखता है कि दो ऑब्जेक्ट एक चित्र हैं -- इसलिए किसी ऑब्जेक्ट के चारों ओर बनाया गया बॉक्स इमेज और मास्क दोनों के उस क्षेत्र को एक अलग फ़ील्ड के रूप में लिखता है (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.write_recrop`), जो वर्तमान फ़ील्ड के ठीक बाद queue में रखा जाता है, और कई ऑब्जेक्टों वाला मूल curate होने के बजाय ``recropped_originals/`` में भेज दिया जाता है (:func:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.retire_recropped_original`)। जिस बॉक्स की कोई भुजा :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MIN_SIDE` से छोटी हो, या जो पहले से किए गए कट को :data:`spacr.qt.mask_engine.RECROP_MAX_OVERLAP` से अधिक दोहराता हो, वह अस्वीकार किया जाता है; जिन ऑब्जेक्टों को बॉक्स काटता है वे हटा दिए जाते हैं, क्योंकि जिस ऑब्जेक्ट की सीमा वहाँ है जहाँ माउस छोड़ा गया, वह वास्तव में वह ऑब्जेक्ट नहीं है; और बचे हुए लेबल एक से फिर से क्रमांकित किए जाते हैं।

records.context: The probability map runs roughly -12..+8 and the flow components ±5; the intensity image is 16-bit counts. records.context: Newer releases are then added. The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a background execution unit, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.

records.source: Newer releases are then added. The wheel for a release cannot contain its own release note -- the note is written when the GitHub release is published, which is after that wheel is on PyPI -- so a bundled file is always one release behind the build carrying it. After the page is shown, :attr:`refresh_requested` asks the window to read the public releases list on a worker thread, and :meth:`apply_releases` merges whatever comes back in front of the bundled list. Nothing here opens a socket: the panel only asks, and a fetch that fails, is rate-limited, is switched off in Preferences, or simply finds nothing newer leaves the bundled list exactly as it was drawn.
records.translation: फिर नई releases जोड़ी जाती हैं। किसी release के wheel में उसका अपना release note नहीं हो सकता -- note GitHub release प्रकाशित होने पर लिखा जाता है, जो उस wheel के PyPI पर आने के बाद होता है -- इसलिए बंडल की गई फ़ाइल हमेशा उसे ले जाने वाले build से एक release पीछे रहती है। पेज दिखाए जाने के बाद, :attr:`refresh_requested` विंडो से सार्वजनिक releases सूची वर्कर थ्रेड पर पढ़ने को कहता है, और :meth:`apply_releases` जो भी लौटे उसे बंडल की गई सूची के आगे मिला देता है। यहाँ कुछ भी socket नहीं खोलता: पैनल केवल माँगता है, और जो fetch विफल हो, rate-limited हो, Preferences में बंद हो, या बस कुछ नया न पाए, वह बंडल की गई सूची को ठीक वैसा ही छोड़ देता है जैसा वह बनी थी।
